answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by tying each identity to a costly, slow-to-build reputation. A new agent starts with no standing, and its votes or attestations only carry weight after it accumulates a history of verified work. Every sockpuppet must therefore pay the full cost of building trust again, and a sudden pulse of fresh identities gets discounted until they earn a zenith of credibility. Plume-like bursts of cheap accounts stay worthless, which makes mass impersonation expensive.
